SealSuite's Network Access Control (NAC) helps enterprises build secure Wi\-Fi and wired networks. You can configure employee Wi\-Fi or wired networks to allow corporate devices or headless terminals to connect to the enterprise network. Additionally, you can set up a guest network to provide temporary network access for visitors. Once personal or corporate devices are connected to the enterprise Wi\-Fi or wired network, you can centrally manage all connected devices from the Admin Console.

<span id="节点部署建议与要求"></span>
# Server deployment recommendations and requirements

If your enterprise purchases SealSuite services with VPN or Wi\-Fi management functions, the initialization process involves the deployment of VPN or RADIUS servers, as shown in the diagram below. For RADIUS servers, internal ACs or switches can access UDP ports 1812/1813/3812/3813/2812/2813. The actual port number shall prevail.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="825px" />

When adding a RADIUS server in SealSuite, you need to prepare a server locally and deploy and install the RADIUS component inside the server to make it a RADIUS server. To ensure the stability of enterprise networks, SealSuite provides the following recommendations and requirements for server configuration and network.

<span id="RADIUS 服务器资源配置参考"></span>
## RADIUS server configuration references

The configuration references of the server are shown in the following table. QPS represents the number of authenticated users per second. A QPS of 300/s means that 300 users can be authenticated per second. If there are 400 users, 100 users will queue up to the next second for authentication, ensuring that previously authenticated users are not affected.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">It's recommended to deploy the SealSuite RADIUS server with a brand new server so as to avoid conflicts with other running application services that cause unexpected network forwarding issues.</div>



| **(Recommended) Operating System Version** |**Configuration** |**QPS** |
|---|---|---|
|CentOS 7, Debian 9, and above |2 core CPU<br><br>2 G memory |300/s |
||4 core CPU<br><br>4 G memory |600/s |
||8 core CPU<br><br>8 G memory |1000/s |


<span id="网络要求"></span>
## Network requirements


* IP address requirements



|**Server** |**Open to the public network?**  |**Example IP Adddress** |**Quantity** |**Notes** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|RADIUS Server |It is recommended to open it to the corporate intranet only. |192.168.1.3 |N, subject to the number of servers in your purchase. |Fixed extranet or intranet IP address. |



* Open port requirements



|**Destination IP** |**Destination Port** |**Protocol** |**Source IP** |**Can it be modified?**  |**Note** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|RADIUS Server IP |1812 |UDP |Wireless Controller |Yes |Employee Wi\-Fi authentication ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wireless controller communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |
||1813 |UDP |Wireless Controller |Yes |Employee Wi\-Fi accounting ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wireless controller communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |
||3812 |UDP |Wireless Controller |Yes |Guest Network authentication ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wireless controller communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |
||3813 |UDP |Wireless Controller |Yes |Guest Network accounting ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wireless controller communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |
||2812 |UDP |Cable switch |Yes |Wired network authentication ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wired switch communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |
||2813 |UDP |Cable switch |Yes |Wired network accounting ports are open to the corporate intranet. If the RADIUS server and wired switch communicate through the internet, they are also open to the internet. |


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">The RADIUS servers need to access the TCP 443 port of the SealSuite tenant domain. Therefore, if your RADIUS server has strict firewall rules that restrict outbound traffic, you need to allow the TCP 443 port in the outbound rules and specify the IP address as the one corresponding to the SealSuite tenant domain name resolution.</div>
